references.text: God's promise to Abraham that his descendants would become as numerous as the stars in the sky, which is the fulfillment Moses refers to in Deuteronomy 1:10.
God's confirmation of the promise to Abraham after he was willing to sacrifice Isaac, where the descendants are compared to the stars in the sky.
God repeats the promise to Isaac that his descendants will become as numerous as the stars in the sky.
God's promise to Jacob that he would become a great nation, showing the continuity of the promise of many descendants.
The description of how the children of Israel became fruitful and multiplied greatly in Egypt, demonstrating the fulfillment of the promise.
Moses reminds God of the promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Israel that their descendants would become as numerous as the stars in the sky.
Moses confirms that God has made the people as numerous as the stars in the sky, from seventy individuals to a great nation.
A warning that those who were as numerous as the stars in the sky will become few if they do not obey the Lord.
Nehemiah refers to God's promise to Abraham of descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky in his prayer.
The book of Hebrews refers to the fulfillment of the promise that Abraham's descendants became as numerous as the stars in the sky, from one man who was as good as dead.
